note: Nomination-day report for the nineteen electoral divisions of Dungannon rural district, one member each. Fifteen candidates were returned unopposed; no nominations were received for Altmore, Clonavaddy, Coalisland and Donaghmore, which were filled by co-option. There was no contest and no poll. Sole nomination; returned unopposed. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page image of Mid-Ulster Mail, 19 April 1924, p. 5 (council-audit, Nov 2026): 'Thomas Girans' -> Thomas Givans, as printed. Renamed from 'Anahoe' to Aghnahoe (13 Nov 2026, by the owner's rule for division spellings: the official or DED-map name where there is one, otherwise the spelling most rounds use): the 1948 order naming Dungannon Rural District's nineteen divisions (Ministry of Health and Local Government, 26 August 1948; Belfast Gazette, 1 April 1949), the DED maps (AGHNAHOE) and the OSNI townland spell it Aghnahoe. This round was filed under the spelling 'Anahoe', a form of the division's name it keeps as an alias; the old address (anahoe) answers with a redirect to this one.
